full_text_en:
Li Jiangui — case of intentional injury

Procuratorial Authority: People's Procuratorate of Changji City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Defendant: Li Jiangui, male, born on June 15, 1977, from Changji City, Xinjiang, farmer. Arrested on February 19, 1998.

The People's Procuratorate of Changji City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, initiated a public prosecution against defendant Li Jiangui for intentional injury, and filed the case with the Changji City People's Court.

The indictment alleged: The defendant Li Jiangui intentionally injured another person with a brick, causing death, and his conduct violated the provisions of Article 234, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law of the PRC, constituting the crime of intentional injury (causing death). To protect citizens' personal rights from illegal infringement, a public prosecution is hereby initiated, and punishment according to law is requested.

Defendant Li Jiangui argued: I originally did not want to help my brother fight. It was my brother who said that at the drinking table, when he was collecting a debt for me, Wen Xiwei not only refused to pay but also hit him, and he asked me to go to save face for him, so I went. After arriving, I learned that it was my brother's fault for being cheating at drinking that caused the fight. I was very angry and told my brother to go home. He not only refused to go home but continued to argue with others. Under these circumstances, to stop him, I threw the brick in my hand at him. At that moment, his head moved, and it happened to hit his head. After I helped him home, his body was limp, like usual drunkenness, so I did not pay attention. Only the next morning did I find he had died. If I had known he would die from this, I would have sent him to the hospital earlier. Although my act caused my brother's death, it was truly not intentional; I request a lenient sentence.

The Changji City People's Court found through trial:

At approximately 10:00 p.m. on February 1, 1998, the defendant Li Jiangui's elder brother Li Jianjun, while drinking at the home of fellow villager Guo Jianwen, had a dispute with villager Wen Xiwei for some reason and was punched by Wen. Li Jianjun then went home and called Li Jiangui to help him fight. Li Jiangui followed Li Jianjun to Guo's home, picked up two bricks at the door, entered the room and saw Wen Xiwei holding an empty wine bottle, so he threw one of the bricks at Wen, hitting Wen in the face and causing minor injury. At this point, Guo Jianwen stopped Li Jiangui and explained that it was Li Jianjun's fault that Wen had hit him. After hearing this, Li Jiangui rebuked Li Jianjun: "It's all your fault, why don't you go home quickly." At that time, Li Jianjun was drunk, refused to listen, and continued to argue. Li Jiangui then threw the other brick at Li Jianjun, hitting him on the head. Afterwards, Li Jiangui and others helped Li Jianjun home to rest. At approximately 7:00 a.m. the next morning, Li Jianjun was found dead at home. Forensic examination: Li Jianjun died from acute subdural hematoma caused by blunt force, leading to respiratory failure.

The above facts are confirmed by physical evidence, witness testimony, forensic examination conclusions, and the defendant Li Jiangui's confession and defense.

Additionally, the villagers' committee of the village where defendant Li Jiangui resides sent a letter to the judicial authorities, stating that Li Jiangui had always behaved well in the past. After Li Jiangui was arrested, his father died of a heart attack, leaving only a mentally disabled mother and a minor brother still in school, and the family is indeed in financial difficulty. They recommended lenient punishment for Li Jiangui.

The Changji City People's Court held that:

After learning that his elder brother Li Jianjun was causing trouble while drunk, the defendant Li Jiangui rebuked him and told him to go home. Because Li Jianjun did not leave, Li Jiangui, in anger, threw the brick in his hand at Li Jianjun, causing head injury, and Li Jianjun died after returning home. Although the consequence of Li Jianjun's death was not what Li Jiangui desired, this targeted injurious act was clearly intentional. Article 234 of the Criminal Law of the PRC provides: "Whoever intentionally injures another person's body shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention, or public surveillance." "Whoever commits the crime in the preceding paragraph, causing serious injury, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years; if causing death or causing serious injury with extreme cruelty resulting in severe disability, the sentence shall be fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years, life imprisonment, or death. Where this Law otherwise provides, follow those provisions." Li Jiangui's conduct violated the provisions of paragraph 2 of this Article, constituting the crime of intentional injury (causing death), and according to law, he should be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years, life imprisonment, or death. His defense that it was not intentional cannot stand. In view of Li Jiangui's truthful confession of his criminal conduct after the crime and his good attitude of admission of guilt, and given the special circumstances of this case, in accordance with the provisions of Article 63, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law, Li Jiangui may be given a mitigated punishment. Based on Li Jiangui's criminal circumstances and his expression of repentance, a suspended sentence may also be applied to him in accordance with Article 72 of the Criminal Law. Accordingly, the court rendered the following judgment on May 26, 1998:

Defendant Li Jiangui is guilty of intentional injury (causing death) and is sentenced to three years' imprisonment, suspended for five years.

After the first instance judgment was pronounced, the defendant Li Jiangui did not appeal, and the procuratorial authority did not file a protest. The Changji City People's Court then reported the case level by level for approval.

During the review by the Changji Hui Autonomous Prefecture Intermediate People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, there was an opinion that when the defendant Li Jiangui threw the brick, he should have foreseen that it might cause the harmful result of Li Jianjun's death, but due to his anger, he did not foresee that result. According to Article 15, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, which provides: "A person who should have foreseen that his act might produce harmful consequences to society but failed to do so due to negligence, or who foresaw such consequences but lightly believed they could be avoided, resulting in such consequences, constitutes a negligent crime," Li Jiangui should be convicted of negligent homicide. In accordance with Article 233 of the Criminal Law, which provides: "Whoever negligently causes death shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than seven years; if the circumstances are minor, the sentence shall be fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years," it was suggested that Li Jiangui be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, while also imposing a suspended sentence. However, the majority of this court still considered the opinion of the Changji City People's Court to be correct, and thus decided to report for approval according to law.

The High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region reviewed and held that the harmful result to society in this case—namely, Li Jianjun's death from injury—was certainly not within the anticipation of the defendant Li Jiangui. Based on Li Jiangui's level of knowledge and the specific circumstances of this case, such a harmful consequence was not something Li Jiangui should have foreseen in advance. Therefore, this case does not constitute a negligent crime. However, before Li Jiangui threw the brick at Li Jianjun, he should have known that such an act would cause injury to Li Jianjun. Due to his anger, he adopted an attitude of indifference toward the occurrence of the injury. Article 14 of the Criminal Law provides: "Whoever knowingly commits an act that will produce harmful consequences to society, and hopes for or is indifferent to the occurrence of such consequences, thus constituting a crime, is an intentional crime." "An intentional crime shall bear criminal responsibility." The first instance court's conviction of Li Jiangui for intentional injury (causing death) and application of Article 63 of the Criminal Law in sentencing was correct.

The Supreme People's Court reviewed and held that:

The defendant Li Jiangui struck Li Jianjun with a brick, causing his death, and his conduct constituted the crime of intentional injury. The facts found by the first instance judgment are clear, the conviction is accurate, and the application of law is appropriate.

The victim in this case bore some fault in the origin of the case. Li Jiangui committed the crime while trying to dissuade the victim from causing trouble while drunk but was rejected by the victim. The means and circumstances of the intentional injury were ordinary, his subjective attitude of indifference toward the injury was minor, and he sincerely repented after the crime. Looking at his subjective culpability and the social harmfulness of the crime, it meets the "special circumstances" provided for in Article 63, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law. Although Li Jiangui does not have a statutory mitigating circumstance, applying Article 63, paragraph 2 to sentence him below the statutory penalty and imposing a suspended sentence is consistent with the basic principle of suiting punishment to crime under China's criminal law. The first instance judgment correctly applied the law, the sentence was appropriate, and the trial procedure was lawful. Accordingly, the Supreme People's Court, in accordance with Article 270 of this Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC, ruled on August 15, 2000:

Approves the criminal judgment of the Changji City People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region imposing a sentence of three years' imprisonment, suspended for five years, on defendant Li Jiangui for the crime of intentional injury, below the statutory penalty.
